title: decision: partial_context_hash concatenates the TLS encodings, length prefix included
description:
Mark 2026-11-26: guess the Right Thing and go with it. Item 5 of bead
mimid-1wgh.44.22, held for posting to the author.

## The ambiguity

semiprivatemessage-08 §3.1 L236:

  partial_context_hash = hash(sender_leaf_index || nonce)

Both fields come from PerMessageKeyAndNonces, where they are
`uint32 sender_leaf_index` and `opaque nonce<V>`. The draft does not say
how the concatenation is encoded. Two readings:

1. The TLS encoding of each field: the index big-endian over four
   octets, the nonce with its `<V>` length prefix.
2. The raw values: the index big-endian over four octets, the nonce's
   bytes alone.

## Chosen: reading 1, the TLS encodings

The hash binds a decryption context, so it has to be injective over
(index, nonce) pairs. Reading 2 is not: with the nonce's length dropped,
the input is a flat byte string, and a different (index, nonce) pair can
produce the same bytes whenever a nonce absorbs what looked like part of
the index -- the index is fixed-width here, so the collision needs a
crafted nonce, but nothing in the draft fixes the nonce's length, and a
context hash that depends on no field being resizable is a sharp edge
for no gain.

Reading 1 is also what "||" over fields of a TLS struct conventionally
means elsewhere in MLS: the encoded form, which is self-delimiting.

## What mimid does

`partial_context_hash` is `hash(PerMessageKeyAndNonces.sender_leaf_index
|| PerMessageKeyAndNonces.nonce)` with each field serialized as
tls_codec writes it: four octets big-endian, then the nonce's length
prefix and its bytes. The hash is the group's ciphersuite hash, since
§3.1 names no other and every other hash in the draft is the
ciphersuite's.

An external receiver that computes it the other way simply fails to
verify, which is a visible failure rather than a silent one, so a wrong
guess here costs interop and not security.

## Still to put to the author

Bead mimid-1wgh.44.22 item 5 stays open: the draft should state the
encoding. It should also say which hash, though the ciphersuite's is the
only reading that makes sense.
